messages:
alex: Quick alert 50 deploy last night (driver 470.86 + kernel bump) correlated with a bunch of failing A100 training jobs in us-west-2.

maya: What errors are we seeing? stack traces or kernel logs?

alex: Example from node kernel log:
```
[ 2345.111111] nvidia: p2p PCIe peer-to-peer disabled for GPU 0000:82:00.0 (BAR1 size insufficient)
[ 2345.111300] nv_peer_mem: peer memory registration failed: -22
[ 2345.112000] NCCL ERROR Call to cudaHostRegister failed; NCCL version 2.10.3
```
This popped up right after the OS+driver update rolled to the A100 reserved pools.

ryan: That BAR1 message is the smoking gun. On Ampere we rely on adequate BAR1 mapping for P2P; if the kernel/BIOS negotiation reduces BAR1 the driver refuses P2P.

juan: Reproduced locally: when P2P is off, NCCL falls back to host-path and throughput drops ~3-4x. Our NCCL microbench shows timeouts after a few seconds under multi-GPU allreduce.

tina: Scope? is it all regions or specific nodepools?

alex: Only dedicated A100 nodepools in us-west-2 affected so far (~120 GPUs). Other regions and V100 pools unaffected.

maya: I recall kernel started enforcing PCIe ACS rules in the newer kernel series. Could the kernel now block downstream peer access? That would disable our previous ACS override.

ryan: Exactly. Previously we used pcie_acs_override=downstream in GRUB for P2P across VFs. Newer kernels are stricter and driver 470 also added BAR1 validation that fails if BAR1 < expected.

juan: Short-term mitigations:
- rollback driver to 460.32.03 on affected hosts
- re-enable pcie_acs_override (security risk)
- cordon/drain affected nodes and migrate workloads to other pools/regions

alex: Ops impact: roughly 40 active jobs degraded/failed; runtime budgets blown up and ML teams are hitting quota errors.

maya: I'm tainting the affected nodes to stop new pods landing. Doing evictions for non-critical jobs.

infra-bot: nodepool/usw2-a100-ded-3 tainted: a100-p2p-issue=true by maya at 1760610005

ryan: Preferred path is rollback driver as it's lowest risk to security. We should canary rollback 3 nodes first and run the NCCL bench.

juan: I can run the canary. Also recommend adding a CI regression: run NCCL P2P smoke on an A100-style test instance whenever drivers or kernels change.

alex: Agree. Ops plan:
1) taint nodes (maya) 
2) canary rollback on 3 nodes (juan)
3) if canary green, rolling rollback across pool at 10 nodes per 10 minutes (ryan)
4) open long-term ticket for vendor BIOS/kernel/driver alignment

tina: I'll loop in security re: ACS override in case we need an emergency hotspot. Also will notify ML leads about potential 2-3hr maintenance.

infra-bot: playbook/driver-rollback started by alex at 1760610030

deploy-bot: canary job #dr-1760610040 queued for usw2-a100-ded

juan: Canary results: after reverting to 460.32.03, p2p shows enabled, NCCL allreduce latencies back to baseline. No cudaHostRegister errors.

ryan: Sounds good. Proceed with rollback waves but monitor closely. Watch for any nodes that fail to boot driver or show dmesg regressions.

maya: Rolling wave 1 (nodes 1-10) now at 1760610200.

alex: Early metrics: job throughput up ~3x for affected workloads, error rate dropping.

tina: Cost note: the retries and longer runtimes added ~USD 4.2k to today's bill for us-west-2. Capture in incident report.

maya: Post-rollback next steps:
- Add NCCL P2P regression test to infra CI
- Automate tainting on driver/kern mismatch detection
- Create vendor ticket to validate BAR1 sizing or BIOS patch on A100 SKUs

ryan: Medium-term: consider scheduling/topology strategies to avoid cross-pci reliance for critical ML jobs and explore RDMA/shmipc fallbacks where possible.

alex: I'll open the incident (a100-p2p-bar1-176061) and assign follow-ups. Juan/Ryan work on a driver patch option that relaxes BAR1 checks; Maya owns CI/test automation; Tina coordinates security/vendor outreach.

infra-bot: incident/1760610001 created: a100-p2p-bar1-regression by alex

alex: Thanks everyone. I'll update the incident ticket with timelines and close out when rollback completes.
